steps.body: Use a line plot for number measurements. Put one X above the value of each measurement.
steps.narration: Use a line plot for number measurements. Put one X above the value of each measurement.

widget.prompt: Votes for four trip spots — a category question. Build the fitting display.
widget.successFeedback: Bars fit votes: one per choice, tops on their counts — categories compared at a glance.
widget.partialFeedback: One bar per choice, each top exactly on its vote count.

predict.prompt: Twenty ribbon lengths, measured to the nearest cm. Which display?
predict.reveal: Twenty bars would name every ribbon; the line plot instead shows which LENGTHS repeat — the actual question.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2g choose graph.
invariants: A display and its data are the same information in two forms: every measurement appears exactly once, and counts survive the trip into stacks, rows, and bars for g2g choose graph.
misconceptions: Reading a label as a count, dropping repeats while recording, or comparing categories by adding instead of finding the gap.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change to the data would the display be FORCED to show — and what change could it silently hide?

widget.prompt: You measure pencil lengths and want to see which lengths repeat. Which display fits?

options.label: A line plot of pencil lengths
options.feedback: Correct — a line plot stacks repeated measurements above number values.

options.label: A bar graph of pencil colors
options.feedback: Color categories do not show which measured lengths repeat.

options.label: A clock showing times
options.feedback: A clock displays time, not repeated pencil lengths.

options.label: A ruler for one pencil
options.feedback: One ruler measurement does not display the whole data set.

options.feedback: The stack above 5 inches has only two Xs.

options.label: 7 inches
options.feedback: The stack above 7 inches has only three Xs.

options.label: 6 inches
options.feedback: Correct — the tallest stack, with four Xs, stands above 6 inches.

widget.prompt: Friday has 3 votes and Saturday has 11 votes. How many more votes on Saturday?

commonErrors.feedback: That put the days TOGETHER — "how many more" asks for the gap between the bars.
11 is Saturday's whole count; the question wants only its lead over Friday.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Subtract the smaller category count from the larger category count to find the gap.
